I tried both. Version A feels much more natural — as I type each label and press Enter, it becomes its own little pill right there in the box with a small x to remove it, so I can see exactly which labels I've added and drop one before saving. Both showed "CSS" and "Reference" as pills on the saved card afterward, but the comma-typing in version B felt more error-prone; I wasn't sure if a stray space or comma would trip it up. So let's go with A.

Your assumptions match mine — labels are short reusable names, I can remove them while editing, and they show as pills on the card.

One important thing I'd want added to this, since it's the whole point of labels being "reusable": as I start typing a label, I'd like it to suggest ones I've already used and let me pick from them. Otherwise I'll end up with "reference" and "Reference" and "refs" all meaning the same thing, and my labels stop being useful. So when I type "Re…", it should offer my existing "Reference" so I reuse it rather than making a near-duplicate. That's the piece missing from what I see here.

Looking forward to seeing what clicking a label does next.
